name: Habit loop

pinned_evidence.title: How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world
pinned_evidence.reason: foundational — Lally et al., 66-day field study

pinned_evidence.title: The habitual consumer
pinned_evidence.reason: review — Wood & Neal on habit mechanisms in behavior

evidence.basis: Habits form through context-dependent repetition until behavior becomes automatic (Lally et al. 2009, ~66-day field study; Wood & Rünger 2016 Annual Review). Cue-triggered automaticity is the well-supported core; the popular 'cue-routine-reward loop' is a useful framing of it.
evidence.effect_size_note: Habit formation is real and field-validated, but slow (weeks to months) and highly dependent on stable context cues and consistent repetition; the '21 days' folk claim is false (median ~66 days, wide range).

mechanism_summary_for_context: Behavior becomes automatic when repeated in a stable context: a consistent cue triggers the action with decreasing conscious effort. The lever for products is building a reliable cue (a consistent trigger — time, notification, entry point) tied to a low-friction action and a genuine reward, repeated until return becomes automatic rather than deliberate. Distinct from variable reward (VR-02 is one possible reward component) — HA-04 is the full cue->action->reward->repetition cycle that produces automaticity.

preconditions.reason: habits require a repeatable core action; not applicable to one-time or infrequent-use products

applicability.culture_note: Habit mechanics are universal; appropriate cue types and cadence (notification norms, daily rhythms) are L3 surface parameters

implementations.generation_directive: Establish one consistent, predictable cue for the core action — same time, same entry point, same trigger — so repetition builds automaticity. Consistency matters more than intensity; a reliable gentle cue beats loud irregular ones. Tie the cue to the user's existing routine where possible.

Make the core habitual action as low-friction as possible — fewest steps from cue to completion, sensible defaults, resumable state. Automaticity forms fastest when the action is easy to perform on cue. Remove decisions that force conscious effort each time.
copy_formulas: Pick up where you left off

hard_rules.rule: The habitual action must deliver real user value; do not build habits around actions that serve engagement metrics but not the user
Cues must be helpful reminders, not manipulative or high-frequency nagging; respect notification limits and user control over cues
Do not engineer habit loops that the user cannot easily stop or that work against their stated intent; habit support, not compulsion

constraints.boundary_test: Is this building a habit the user wants and benefits from — or engineering compulsive return against their interest?

relations.note: Variable reward can be the reward component of a habit loop; HA-04 is the full cue-action-reward-repetition cycle, VR-02 is one reward strategy within it
Progress and streaks support habit maintenance; distinct — ZE-07 is goal-directed progress, HA-04 is context-cued automaticity

reference_examples.what: Consistent time-based cue + low-friction lesson builds a daily-return habit; the streak (ZE-07/LA-01) reinforces an already-cued routine
Once-daily cadence + same simple action + social share creates a strong daily habit with minimal mechanics
Consistent daily meditation cue tied to routine (morning/bedtime) builds automaticity around a genuinely valued action
